paragraphs: Children in care in Yorkshire are looked after by the county's councils, each with its own fostering service, and by the independent fostering agencies listed on this page. In May 2024 councils across Yorkshire and the Humber said the region needed about 1,000 new foster carers, with more children coming into care than ever before. North Yorkshire said that, on its own, it needs around 300 fostering families at any one time.

The councils have worked together on recruitment for several years. In 2021 Bradford, Calderdale, Hull, Kirklees, Leeds, North Yorkshire, Wakefield and York launched Foster4YourCouncil, a joint partnership with shared online events, noting reports that the number of children needing a safe home could rise by a third by 2030. In 2024 seven councils, including East Riding of Yorkshire, made a short film together for Foster Care Fortnight to show what fostering is really like.

The councils say there is no typical foster carer, welcome people from every background, and look for both full-time and part-time carers. Their carers receive a weekly fee and allowance alongside ongoing training and support.

Yorkshire is a big place, so look at the page for your own city or council area too, such as Leeds, Bradford, Sheffield or York. Speak to your council and to two or three of the agencies below, and ask each about the ages of children they most need homes for, the training and support they give, and what they pay, before you choose.

sources.title: Film launched as 1,000 new foster carers urgently needed (North Yorkshire Council, 14 May 2024)
Yorkshire councils unite for vital push on fostering (Leeds City Council, 2021)
